# linux-computer-use

> An open source computer use agent for Linux: an MCP server that lets Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or any MCP client drive a real browser on your own Linux machine, with a live view, human takeover, and safety guardrails.

Self-hosted browser automation for AI agents on Linux, an alternative to cloud-hosted computer use products. Node.js MCP server wrapping playwright-cli. Launches the bundled Chromium, or Chrome, Firefox, WebKit and Edge, and attaches over CDP to any Chromium-based browser you started yourself (Brave, Opera, Vivaldi). It also drives native Linux applications (Burp Suite, Wireshark, Ghidra) in a nested X desktop of its own, which needs Xephyr, xdotool, ImageMagick and a window manager. Requires Linux, Node.js 20+, and a graphical session (DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY). Licensed MIT. Owner: Roadmvn.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Roadmvn/linux-computer-use/blob/main/README.md): what it is, install, use your own browser, tool reference, comparison with other computer use agents, FAQ
- [Design notes](https://github.com/Roadmvn/linux-computer-use/blob/main/docs/design.md): architecture, control lease between agent and human, guardrails, audit trail, desktop backend and why it uses a nested X display
- [Repository](https://github.com/Roadmvn/linux-computer-use): source, issues, releases

## Install

- [install.sh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roadmvn/linux-computer-use/main/scripts/install.sh): one-line installer, run with `curl -fsSL <url> | bash`

Register with a client:

The installer places the server in `~/.linux-computer-use/app` and prints these:

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user linux-computer-use -- node ~/.linux-computer-use/app/src/index.js`
- OpenAI Codex: `codex mcp add linux-computer-use -- node ~/.linux-computer-use/app/src/index.js`

## MCP tools

- `open`: open a browser session, or attach to one already running (url, session, profile, browser, cdp)
- `goto`: navigate to a URL (url)
- `snapshot`: accessibility tree of the page with element refs
- `screenshot`: image capture of the page
- `click`: click an element by ref (ref, confirm)
- `type`: type text (text)
- `fill`: fill a field by ref (ref, text)
- `press`: press a key (key)
- `mouse`: mouse by coordinates, vision mode (action, x, y, confirm)
- `tabs`: manage tabs (action: list, new, select, close; index, url)
- `history`: history navigation (direction: back, forward, reload)
- `status`: session and control lease state, hands control to the human (takeover)
- `set_mode`: switch between normal and auto mode (mode)

Desktop backend, native applications in a nested X display:

- `desktop_start`: start the agent desktop, required before the other desktop tools (width, height, stop)
- `desktop_windows`: list the visible windows with id, title, class and geometry
- `desktop_focus`: bring a window to the front (id)
- `desktop_screenshot`: capture the desktop, or a single window (window)
- `desktop_click`: move the pointer and click (x, y, button, move_only)
- `desktop_type`: type text into the focused window (text, confirm)
- `desktop_key`: press a key or combination, e.g. Return, ctrl+c, alt+Tab (key, confirm)
- `desktop_launch`: start an application from the desktop catalog (app, confirm)

## Features

- live view: run `npx playwright-cli show` yourself for a window on this machine, or `npx playwright-cli show --port=7777 --host=0.0.0.0` to reach it from another machine. The server never starts it
- human takeover: the agent hands over with `status {takeover: true}`, which creates `~/.linux-computer-use/lease`. Every agent action is refused while that file exists, and only the human can delete it
- use your own browser: start it with `--remote-debugging-port` and a separate `--user-data-dir`, then attach with `cdp`. Since Chromium 136 the debugging port is ignored on the default profile
- visible agent cursor drawn on the page, following the agent's own actions only
- named isolated sessions, cookies kept between runs only when `profile` is set
- act by accessibility tree (robust) or by pixel coordinates, both checked by the same guardrails
- guardrails fail closed: no credential entry, stops on empty login forms and account choices, confirms irreversible actions, refuses when the target or the page cannot be read
- audit log of counters only, never field values or keys, URLs reduced to their origin
- normal mode confirms before committing a form, auto mode does not, both stop on credentials and irreversible actions
- native applications in a nested X display (Xephyr from :20, xfwm4, 1280x800 by default), so the agent never takes the pointer or the focus from the human: on a shared display xdotool drives the single core pointer, and input sent to a background window through XSendEvent is ignored by modern toolkits
- applications keep their per-user configuration, so Burp Suite started there has the same settings, extensions and CA as usual; the desktop is detached and its display is recorded in `~/.linux-computer-use/desktop.json`, so a server restart reattaches instead of opening a second one
- desktop guardrails are thinner by design: allowlist of applications (`LCU_APPS`), confirm required when a terminal has focus, and the same lease, but no check by element name because there is no accessibility tree, only pixels. AT-SPI is on the roadmap

## Related

- [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io): the protocol the server implements
- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev): the browser automation stack it builds on
